tone_statements.quote: Tone on individual words is normally not written. Except for some nouns that make the difference between singular and plural with different tone. In that case the plural is written with a relative high tone mark on the first vowel: biosu a fish bíosu many fish [...] Minimal pairs To distinguish some minimal tone pairs, words with the same sounds but different tone, certain words are spelled in a different way to avoid confusion: bɔ́ up bɔ them bɛŋŋ my bəŋ this nɨŋ work nɨŋŋ refuse diɔ sun diɔ́ day llə cross lə that kkə know kə beat

Mbɔndu bə Ntanchɛ Kɨŋwatɨ Diɛ yi Bədzumbu lə Ntɨŋ [Reading and Writing the Kemedzung Language]. First edition. Cameroon: Kemedzung Language Committee. 83 pp. (Kemedzung transition primer; SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 48160.)
tone_statements.quote: The Kemedzung language has one group of nouns that shows the difference between singular and plural simply by the tone or pitch of the words. So, the spelling is the same in the singular and in the plural. In order to show the difference in the words on paper, we will mark the plural form with a diacritic that slants upward ‟ ́‟ above the first vowel in the word, as you can see from the key words and exercises that follow. shə „fowl‟ shə́ „fowls‟ … tsɔŋ „house‟ tsɔ́ŋ „houses‟ bi „goat‟ bí „goats‟ biɔsu „fish‟ bíɔsu „fish‟ shiŋ „sheep‟ shíŋ „sheep‟ dzowa „mushroom‟ dzówa „mushrooms‟
tone_statements.locator: booklet p. 51, Lesson Fifteen 'Tone on Singular and Plural Nouns' (pp. 50-53) right half (2-up sheets: p. 50 left, p. 52 left, p. 53 right; answer key p. 70 left)
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Literacy primer: states that one group of nouns marks plural by tone alone, written with an acute on the first vowel (tsɔŋ 'house' / tsɔ́ŋ 'houses', bi / bí 'goat(s)'); no tone inventory or analysis.

tone_statements.citation: Cox, Bruce. 2005. Notes on the Phonology of Kemezung. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. iii+17 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Kemezung has three contrastive tone levels: high, mid and low. Before a pause, low tone is realized falling from low to extra low pitch. High tone is rather rare in monomorphemic words, although it does occur in some grammatical words … Several contour tones are attested in Kemezung. The prevalence of rising and falling9 contour tones in short words, particularly monosyllables, and their absence (except word-finally) in longer words suggests that, as in many African languages, they are to be analyzed as sequences of level tones.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2.4.1 Level tones and 2.4.2 Contour tones, p. 7

sources.note: The 'Language > Phonology' page is an orthography summary explicitly based on Cox 2005 (Kemezung orthography guide) plus a minor phoneme /p/. On tone it states that tone on individual words is normally not written, except that some nouns distinguish singular from plural by tone alone, the plural then being written with a high tone mark on the first vowel (biosu 'a fish' vs. bíosu 'many fish' -- i.e. grammatical number marked by tone), and that lexical minimal tone pairs exist and are disambiguated by ad hoc spellings (bɔ́ 'up' vs bɔ 'them', nɨŋ 'work' vs nɨŋŋ 'refuse', diɔ 'sun' vs diɔ́ 'day'…
